Work Your Magic with us! Start your next chapter and join EMD Electronics.

Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Location:
The Head of Global Customer Quality is a remote role from US, Korea or Taiwan.
Travel

Your Role
As the Global Customer Quality Manager, you will drive Customer Quality engagement for our customers across all Business Units (BUs) in the Electronics division. In this role, you will collaborate closely with the Global Key Account Managers (GKAMs) and Account Teams to nurture customer relationships and deliver exceptional performance and results. You will serve as the vital communication bridge between EMD Electronics and our customers, ensuring their needs are understood and addressed while advancing their technology. Additionally, you will represent the Voice of the Customer for Quality to internal stakeholders, playing a crucial role in aligning our services with customer expectations and fostering long-term partnerships.

Develop and lead our proactive Customer Quality engagement strategy with a focus on strategic customers to drive customer systems collaboration, customer scorecard optimization, and customer quality roadmap engagement.
Act as the second point of escalation for Customer Quality issues.
Develop and mentor a Global Customer Quality Team with an optimal mix of technical and commercial competency.
Drive the development and maintenance of Electronics Customer Quality Roadmaps.
Lead and manage the successful completion of Customer Quality Initiatives and Programs across all Electronics businesses.
Drive team ownership of customer engagement between Electronics and customers for Quality issues.

Ensure facilitation of Customer Quality Audits to drive preparation, enhance performance, and ensure follow-up and closure.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, or other technical disciplines with 8+years of manufacturing, business, and quality experience in a fast-paced time sensitive environment.

Confidence interacting with customers and senior internal leaders.
Demonstrated leadership and coaching experience with global teams.
Excellent communication skills (English) – oral and written.
Ability to collaborate with people from various backgrounds/cultures/functions in a highly matrixed global organization.
Excellent time management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple activities, projects, and demands independently.
Semiconductor fab experience
Significant commercial negotiation experience
Moderate Statistical knowledge
Experience in Quality tools for problem solving (5 Why, Model Based Problem Solving), FMEAs, Continuous Improvement (CI) activities, Management of Change (MOC), and Document Control systems.
Experience with ISO9001 Quality Management Systems
SAP experience

The Director Electrical BOP Engineering, Operations
, supports RWE America's renewable generation assets by managing the team focusing specifically on balance of plant (BOP) equipment and systems. The Electrical BOP team provides engineering expertise for a wide range of BOP components, such as transformers, cables, dynamic and static reactive power devices, substations, relays, breakers, and power plant controllers. By collaborating closely with teams in Operations, Asset Management, Compliance, and Development/Construction, the Electrical BOP team helps ensure that current and future generating assets consistently operate at their best.
We are seeking a strategic engineering leader with deep expertise in high-voltage infrastructure and utility-scale electrical Balance of Plant (BOP) architecture. The ideal candidate combines authoritative technical expertise with strong executive presence—equally skilled at setting multiyear fleet reliability strategies, navigating complex NERC/FERC compliance landscapes, and building high-performing engineering teams. You bring a strong owner-operator mindset, excel at cross-functional alignment across field operations and development, and thrive at translating technical electrical risk into actionable business decisions.

Define engineering vision, standards, and goals across the renewable generation fleet. Translate business objectives into technical action
Shape multiyear investment plans for substation upgrades, reliability enhancements, and compliance readiness
Oversee NERC/FERC audit preparedness and evidence reviews. Establish frameworks for continuous improvement and documentation rigor
Define the org structure, span of control, and career pathing for the Electrical BOP function. Sponsor key talent and hiring efforts
Represent engineering to executive leadership. Align initiatives with Asset Management, Field Operations, and Compliance
Evaluate and champion adoption of new engineering tools, modeling platforms, or controls testing technologies
Assess electrical risk and integration effort for acquired sites. Standardize onboarding of models, settings, and testing procedures
Define thresholds for technical sign-off, model review, and restoration support across the engineering team
Lead technical forensic investigations, Root Cause Analyses (RCAs), and major failure recovery efforts for critical fleet assets (e.g., main power transformers, HV breakers, dynamic VAR systems)
Oversee technical relationships with major equipment OEMs, engineering consultants, and testing contractors; establish standardized technical specifications and quality control guidelines for fleet repairs and retrofits

Bachelor of Science or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering (EE) required (or equivalent deep experience in high-voltage power systems engineering)
Professional Engineer (PE) preferred

HV/EHV & Grid Interconnection Experience
Detailed knowledge of power generation and distribution equipment, transformers, switchgear, transmission feeders, substations, and renewable energy

Strong understanding of protective device coordination and relay settings
Familiarity with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) standards

Serves as functional leader and internal expert

Leads resolution of complex, ambiguous problems with long-term impacts

This position is an office-based role with some travel and visits to other RWE Americas offices and field locations. The employee must be able to sit, walk, or stand for long durations of time.
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RWE Americas is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.

Job Description


About FIS


Are you curious, motivated, and forward-thinking? At FIS you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and relevant issues in financial services and technology. Our talented people empower us, and we believe in being part of a team that is open, collaborative, entrepreneurial, passionate and above all fun.


Current and future sponsorship are not available for this position


Jacksonville, FL Hybrid (three days in-office, two days virtual)


About the team


The Quality Engineering Platform is part of FIS Developer Experience, the platform engineering group that builds the tools, pipelines and services more than 5,000 FIS engineers use to build, test and ship software. As AI coding assistants and agents write a growing share of our code, the volume of change is climbing fast. Our job is to make sure quality keeps pace, giving every team fast, trustworthy signal on whether a change is safe to release, whether a person or an AI wrote it.


What you will be doing


You will own the direction of the entire Quality Engineering Platform and lead the teams that build it, reporting to the head of Developer Experience platforms. You will decide where the platform goes as AI changes how software is written and tested, turn that into a roadmap teams across FIS want to adopt, and be accountable for the results.


  • Set the vision, strategy and multi-year roadmap for the Quality Engineering Platform, designed for a world where AI writes and tests a large share of our code.
  • Lead and grow the Quality Engineering Platform teams, including early-career engineers, in close partnership with the platform’s Principal Engineer and Delivery Manager.
  • Build quality capabilities for AI-generated code, such as automated test generation, checks that run before code is merged, and ways to measure whether AI tools actually improve outcomes.
  • Drive adoption across FIS engineering teams by making the platform the easiest path to fast, reliable testing, measured by adoption, release confidence and defects that reach clients.
  • Partner with DevSecOps, Developer Experience, observability and AI platform teams so quality is built into the developer workflow from first commit to production.
  • Own the platform’s operating model, including priorities, budget, tool and vendor choices, service levels and the metrics you report to senior leadership.

What you bring


  • Significant experience leading software engineering teams, including leading through managers or technical leads.
  • A track record of owning a platform or product end to end: strategy, roadmap, delivery and adoption by its users.
  • Deep, hands-on understanding of test automation, CI/CD and modern quality practices, enough to challenge technical decisions and earn the trust of senior engineers.
  • Practical experience with AI coding tools such as GitHub Copilot or Claude Code, and a clear point of view on how they change testing and quality.
  • Ability to express quality in numbers leadership cares about (escaped defects, release frequency, recovery time, test reliability) and use them to make decisions.
  • Confident communication with senior stakeholders and a habit of influencing teams you don’t directly manage.

Bonus if you have


  • Experience in financial services or another regulated industry where quality failures carry real client and compliance impact.
  • Experience building or adopting AI-driven testing, such as generated tests, self-healing tests or evaluation of AI agent output.
  • Experience running an internal platform as a product, with user research, adoption metrics and internal customer support.
  • Experience building teams that include early-career engineers or college hire programs.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Playwright, Cypress, k6 or Selenium at enterprise scale.

What we offer you


  • A competitive salary and benefits.
  • A variety of career development tools, resources and opportunities.
  • The chance to work on some of the most challenging, relevant issues. in financial services & technology.
  • Time to support charities and give back in your community.
  • A work environment built on collaboration, flexibility and respect.


Privacy Statement

FIS is committed to protecting the privacy and security of all personal information that we process in order to provide services to our clients. For specific information on how FIS protects personal information online, please see the Online Privacy Notice.
